title.zh: 卷一百四十七 列傳第七十二 三王魯辛馮三李曲二盧
title.en: Volume 147 Biographies 72: Three Wangs, Lu, Xin, Feng, Three Li, Qu, Two Lu's
title.raw: 卷一百四十七 列傳第七十二 三王魯辛馮三李曲二盧 Volume 147 Biographies 72: Three Wangs, Lu, Xin, Feng, Three Li, Qu, Two Lu's

sentences.zh: 三王魯辛馮三李曲二盧

translations.literal: Three Wangs, Lu, Xin, Feng, three Li, Qu, two Lu's.
translations.idiomatic: Three Wangs, Lu, Xin, Feng, three Li, Qu, and two Lu's.

sentences.zh: 王思禮，高麗人，入居營州。

translations.literal: Wang Sili was a man of Goguryeo who entered and settled in Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sili was a native of Goguryeo who had come to live in Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 父為朔方軍將。

translations.literal: His father was a general of the Shuofang Army.
translations.idiomatic: His father served as a general in the Shuofang Army.

sentences.zh: 思禮習戰鬥，從王忠嗣至河西，與哥舒翰同籍麾下。

translations.literal: Sili was practiced in combat; he followed Wang Zhongsi to Hexi and served under the same commander as Geshu Han.
translations.idiomatic: Trained in warfare, Sili followed Wang Zhongsi to Hexi and served in the same command as Geshu Han.

sentences.zh: 翰為隴右節度使，思禮與中郎將周佖事翰，以功授右衛將軍、關西兵馬使。

translations.literal: When Han became military commissioner of Longyou, Sili and the Central Gentleman-General Zhou Ji served Han; for merit he was appointed General of the Right Guard and Guanxi military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Han became commissioner of Longyou, Sili and Central Gentleman-General Zhou Ji served under him; for his achievements he was made General of the Right Guard and military commissioner of Guanxi.

sentences.zh: 從討九曲，後期當斬，臨刑，翰釋之，思禮徐曰：「死固分也，何復貸為？」

translations.literal: In the campaign against Jiuqu he was late and was to be executed; at the execution Han released him. Sili said calmly: "Death is my allotted portion—why grant a reprieve?"
translations.idiomatic: On the campaign against Jiuqu he arrived late and was sentenced to death; as the execution was about to proceed, Han spared him. Sili said calmly, "Death is what I deserve—why spare me?"

sentences.zh: 諸將壯之。

translations.literal: The generals admired him.
translations.idiomatic: The other generals were deeply impressed.

sentences.zh: 天寶十三載，吐谷渾蘇毗王款附，詔翰至磨環川應接，思禮墜馬，蹇甚。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Tianbao, the Tuyuhun Supi king came to submit; the court ordered Han to Mo Huan Chuan to receive him. Sili fell from his horse and was severely lame.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao year 13, when the Tuyuhun Supi king came to submit, the court ordered Han to Mo Huan Chuan to receive him. Sili fell from his horse and was badly crippled.

sentences.zh: 翰謂監軍李文宜曰：「思禮跛足，尚欲何之？」

translations.literal: Han said to the army supervisor Li Wenyi: "Sili is lame—where does he still wish to go?"
translations.idiomatic: Han told army supervisor Li Wenyi, "Sili is lame—where does he think he is going?"

sentences.zh: 俄加金城郡太守。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he was additionally appointed prefect of Jincheng commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was also made prefect of Jincheng.

sentences.zh: 安祿山反，翰為元帥，奏思禮赴軍，玄宗曰：「河、隴精銳，悉在潼關，吐蕃有釁，唯倚思禮耳。」

translations.literal: When An Lushan rebelled, Han was supreme commander and memorialized that Sili should join the army. Emperor Xuanzong said: "The elite troops of He and Long are all at Tong Pass; if Tibet makes trouble, we rely on Sili alone."
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan rebelled, Han was appointed supreme commander and asked that Sili join the campaign. Emperor Xuanzong said, "The crack troops of He and Long are all at Tong Pass; if Tibet stirs trouble, we depend on Sili alone."

sentences.zh: 翰固請，乃兼太常卿，充元帥府馬軍都將，翰委以軍事。

translations.literal: Han pressed his request firmly; then Sili was additionally made Minister of Ceremonies and cavalry commander of the supreme commander's staff, and Han entrusted him with military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Han pressed hard, and Sili was then also made Minister of Ceremonies and cavalry commander on the commander's staff; Han entrusted him with military affairs.

sentences.zh: 密勸翰表誅楊國忠，翰不應；

translations.literal: He secretly urged Han to memorialize for the execution of Yang Guozhong; Han did not agree;
translations.idiomatic: He secretly urged Han to petition for Yang Guozhong's execution; Han refused;

sentences.zh: 復請以三十騎劫至潼關殺之，翰曰：「此乃吾反，何與祿山事？」

translations.literal: he again asked to take thirty horsemen, seize him, bring him to Tong Pass, and kill him. Han said: "That would be my rebellion—what has it to do with Lushan's affair?"
translations.idiomatic: he then proposed taking thirty horsemen to seize Yang and kill him at Tong Pass. Han said, "That would be my rebellion—what does it have to do with Lushan?"

sentences.zh: 潼關失守，思禮與呂崇賁、李承光同走行在，肅宗責不堅守，引至纛下將斬之。

translations.literal: When Tong Pass fell, Sili fled with Lü Chongbin and Li Chengguang to the imperial camp. Emperor Suzong blamed them for not holding firm and had them brought before the command banner to be executed.
translations.idiomatic: When Tong Pass fell, Sili fled with Lü Chongbin and Li Chengguang to the emperor's camp. Suzong blamed them for failing to hold the pass and had them brought before the command banner for execution.

sentences.zh: 宰相房琯諫，以為可收後效，遂獨斬承光，赦思禮等。

translations.literal: The chief minister Fang Guan remonstrated, holding that they could still be used for later effect; thereupon Chengguang alone was executed and Sili and the others were pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Chief minister Fang Guan argued that they could still prove useful later; Chengguang alone was executed, and Sili and the others were spared.

sentences.zh: 尋副房琯戰便橋，不利，更為關內行營節度、河西隴右伊西行營兵馬使，守武功。

translations.literal: Soon he served as Fang Guan's deputy at the battle of Bian Bridge, which went badly; he was then made commissioner of the Guannei field army and military commissioner of the Hexi, Longyou, and Yixi field armies, defending Wugong.
translations.idiomatic: He soon fought under Fang Guan at Bian Bridge, where the army was defeated; he was then made commissioner of the Guannei field army and military commander of the Hexi, Longyou, and Yixi forces, with orders to hold Wugong.

sentences.zh: 賊安守忠來戰，思禮退保扶風。

translations.literal: The rebel An Shouzhong came to give battle; Sili withdrew to defend Fufeng.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebel An Shouzhong attacked, Sili fell back to defend Fufeng.

sentences.zh: 賊分兵略大和關，去鳳翔五十里，李光進戰未利，行在戒嚴，從官潛出其孥，帝使左右巡御史虞候識其姓名，眾稍稍止。

translations.literal: The rebels sent detachments to seize Dahe Pass, fifty li from Fengxiang. Li Guangjin fought without success. The imperial camp was placed under strict guard; attendants secretly sent out their wives and children. The emperor had the Left and Right Patrol Censors record their names, and the crowd gradually ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel detachments seized Dahe Pass, fifty li from Fengxiang. Li Guangjin's attack failed. The imperial camp was placed under martial law as courtiers secretly evacuated their families. The emperor had patrol censors record their names, and the panic slowly subsided.

sentences.zh: 命郭子儀以朔方兵擊之。

translations.literal: He ordered Guo Ziyi to strike them with the Shuofang army.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Guo Ziyi to attack with the Shuofang troops.

sentences.zh: 會崔光遠行軍司馬王伯倫、判官李椿以兵二千屯扶風。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Cui Guangyuan's field army marshal Wang Bolun and aide Li Chun stationed two thousand troops at Fufeng.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Cui Guangyuan's field marshal Wang Bolun and aide Li Chun had two thousand men at Fufeng.

sentences.zh: 聞賊已西，欲乘虛襲京師，徑至高陵。

translations.literal: Hearing that the rebels had gone west, they wished to exploit the opening and strike the capital, going straight to Gaoling.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing the rebels had moved west, they planned to strike the capital while it was exposed and marched straight for Gaoling.

sentences.zh: 賊引軍還擊椿等，椿已至中渭橋，殺守者千人，進攻苑門。

translations.literal: The rebels turned their army back to strike Chun and the others. Chun had already reached the Middle Wei Bridge, killed a thousand defenders, and advanced to attack the park gate.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels turned back to attack Chun's force. Chun had reached the Middle Wei Bridge, killed a thousand defenders, and pressed on toward the imperial park gate.

sentences.zh: 伯倫戰死，椿被執。

translations.literal: Bolun died in battle; Chun was captured.
translations.idiomatic: Bolun was killed in battle and Chun was taken prisoner.

sentences.zh: 先是，賊餘眾留武功，既傳官軍入京師，乃燒營遁，自是賊不敢西。

translations.literal: Earlier, rebel remnants had remained at Wugong; once word spread that government troops had entered the capital, they burned their camp and fled. From then on the rebels did not dare go west.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier rebel remnants had held Wugong; when word spread that imperial troops had entered the capital, they burned their camp and fled. After that the rebels no longer dared move west.

sentences.zh: 長安平，思禮先入清宮；

translations.literal: When Chang'an was pacified, Sili was first to enter and clear the palace;
translations.idiomatic: When Chang'an was recovered, Sili was first to enter and secure the palace;

sentences.zh: 收東京，戰數有功。

translations.literal: in recovering the Eastern Capital he fought repeatedly with merit.
translations.idiomatic: and in retaking the Eastern Capital he won repeated victories.

sentences.zh: 遷兵部尚書，封霍國公，食實戶五百。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of War, enfeoffed as Duke of Huo, with a substantive household of five hundred.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Minister of War, enfeoffed as Duke of Huo, with an income of five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 尋兼潞、沁等州節度。

translations.literal: Soon he was additionally made military commissioner of Lu, Qin, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon also made military commissioner of Lu, Qin, and neighboring prefectures.

sentences.zh: 乾元元年，總關中、潞州行營兵三萬、騎八千，與子儀圍賊相州，軍潰，惟李光弼、思禮完軍還。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianyuan, commanding thirty thousand infantry and eight thousand cavalry of the Guannei and Lu field armies, he joined Guo Ziyi in besieging the rebels at Xiangzhou; the army was routed, but only Li Guangbi and Sili returned with their forces intact.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qianyuan he commanded thirty thousand foot soldiers and eight thousand horsemen from the Guannei and Lu field armies and joined Guo Ziyi in besieging the rebels at Xiangzhou. The army was routed, but only Li Guangbi and Sili brought their forces back intact.

sentences.zh: 尋破史思明別將萬餘眾於直千嶺。

translations.literal: Soon he defeated more than ten thousand of Shi Siming's detached commanders at Zhigan Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: He soon routed more than ten thousand of Shi Siming's detached troops at Zhigan Ridge.

sentences.zh: 光弼徙河陽，代為河東節度副大使。

translations.literal: When Guangbi moved to Heyang, Sili replaced him as deputy military commissioner of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangbi was transferred to Heyang, Sili replaced him as deputy commissioner of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 上元元年，加司空。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shangyuan he was additionally made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shangyuan he was made Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 自武德以來，三公不居宰輔，唯思禮而已。

translations.literal: Since Wude, the Three Dukes had not held posts as chief ministers—only Sili did.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Wude era no one holding one of the Three Excellencies had also served as chief minister—only Sili.

sentences.zh: 二年，薨，贈太尉，謚曰武烈。

translations.literal: In the second year he died; he was posthumously made Grand Preceptor, with the posthumous title Martial and Fierce.
translations.idiomatic: He died in year 2 and was posthumously made Grand Preceptor, with the posthumous title Martial and Fierce.

sentences.zh: 思禮善守計，短攻戰。

translations.literal: Sili was skilled in defensive planning but weak in offensive warfare.
translations.idiomatic: Sili excelled at defensive strategy but was less adept at offensive fighting.

sentences.zh: 然持法嚴整，士不敢犯。

translations.literal: Yet he upheld the law with strict order, and soldiers did not dare offend.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he enforced discipline so strictly that his men did not dare transgress.

sentences.zh: 在太原，器甲完精，儲粟至百萬斛雲。

translations.literal: At Taiyuan, weapons and armor were complete and refined, and stored grain reached a million hu, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: At Taiyuan his arms and armor were kept in perfect order, and grain stores reportedly reached a million hu.

sentences.zh: 魯炅，幽州薊人。

translations.literal: Lu Jiong was a native of Ji in Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Jiong was from Ji in Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 長七尺餘，略通書史。

translations.literal: He stood more than seven chi tall and had some knowledge of books and history.
translations.idiomatic: He stood over seven chi tall and had a modest education in letters and history.

sentences.zh: 以蔭補左羽林長上。

translations.literal: Through hereditary privilege he was appointed senior attendant of the Left Forest Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Through hereditary privilege he entered service as a senior attendant of the Left Forest Guard.

sentences.zh: 隴右節度使哥舒翰引為別奏。

translations.literal: Geshu Han, military commissioner of Longyou, brought him in as a special aide.
translations.idiomatic: Longyou commissioner Geshu Han took him on as a special aide.

sentences.zh: 顏真卿嘗使隴右，謂翰曰：「君興郎將，總節制，亦嘗得人乎？」

translations.literal: Yan Zhenqing once served on mission in Longyou and said to Han: "You rose from a gentleman-captain to hold overall command—have you also found capable men?"
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zhenqing once visited Longyou on official business and asked Han, "You rose from a captain to full command—have you found capable men under you?"

sentences.zh: 炅時立階下，翰指曰：「是當為節度使。」

translations.literal: Jiong was then standing below the steps. Han pointed and said: "This man is fit to be a military commissioner."
translations.idiomatic: Jiong was standing below the steps. Han pointed and said, "That man is destined to be a commissioner."

sentences.zh: 從破石堡城，收河曲，遷左武衛將軍。

translations.literal: He followed in the capture of Stone Fortress City and the recovery of Hequ, and was transferred to General of the Left Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He fought in the capture of Stone Fortress City and the recovery of Hequ, and was promoted to General of the Left Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 後復以破吐蕃跳蕩功，除右領軍大將軍。

translations.literal: Later, again for merit in defeating the Tibetan raiders, he was made Grand General of the Right Forward Army.
translations.idiomatic: Later, for defeating Tibetan raiders, he was made Grand General of the Right Forward Army.

sentences.zh: 安祿山反，拜上洛太守，將行，於帝前畫攻守勢，遷南陽太守，兼守捉防禦使，封金鄉公。

translations.literal: When An Lushan rebelled, he was appointed prefect of Shangluo; before departing he sketched offensive and defensive dispositions before the emperor. He was transferred to prefect of Nanyang, concurrently defense commissioner, and enfeoffed as Duke of Jinxiang.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan rebelled, he was made prefect of Shangluo; before leaving he outlined attack and defense plans before the emperor. He was then transferred to Nanyang as prefect and defense commissioner and enfeoffed as Duke of Jinxiang.

sentences.zh: 尋為山南節度使，以嶺南、黔中、山南東道子弟五萬屯滍水南。

translations.literal: Soon he was made military commissioner of Shannan, stationing fifty thousand youths from Lingnan, Qianzhong, and eastern Shannan south of the Zhi River.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made commissioner of Shannan and stationed fifty thousand recruits from Lingnan, Qianzhong, and eastern Shannan south of the Zhi River.

sentences.zh: 賊將武令珣、畢思琛等擊之，眾欲戰，炅不可。

translations.literal: The rebel generals Wu Lingxun, Bi Sichen, and others attacked; the troops wished to fight, but Jiong would not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel generals Wu Lingxun and Bi Sichen attacked; the men wanted to fight, but Jiong refused.

sentences.zh: 賊右趨，乘風縱火，郁氣奔營，士不可止，負扉走，賊矢如雨，炅與中人薛道挺身走，舉眾沒賊。

translations.literal: The rebels veered right, rode the wind to set fires, and dense smoke rushed into the camp; the soldiers could not be stopped, shouldered the barricade gates and fled. Rebel arrows fell like rain. Jiong and the palace attendant Xue Dao fled at full stride; the whole force was lost to the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels swung right, set fires on the wind, and smoke rolled into the camp. The men could not be held; they shouldered the barricade gates and fled as rebel arrows fell like rain. Jiong and palace attendant Xue Dao fled headlong, and the entire force was overrun.

sentences.zh: 時嶺南節度使何履光、黔中節度使趙國珍、襄陽節度使徐浩未至，其子弟半在軍，挾金為資糧，至是與械偕棄與山等，賊資以富。

translations.literal: At the time the commissioners He Lüguang of Lingnan, Zhao Guozhen of Qianzhong, and Xu Hao of Xiangyang had not yet arrived; half their youths were in the army carrying gold as provisions. Now they abandoned it together with weapons on the hills, and the rebels grew rich from it.
translations.idiomatic: Commissioners He Lüguang of Lingnan, Zhao Guozhen of Qianzhong, and Xu Hao of Xiangyang had not yet arrived; half their recruits were in the army carrying gold as supplies. Now gold and weapons were abandoned on the hills, enriching the rebels.

sentences.zh: 炅揪散兵保南陽。

translations.literal: Jiong gathered scattered troops to hold Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong rallied scattered troops to defend Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 潼關失守，賊使哥舒翰招下，不從，使武令珣攻之。

translations.literal: When Tong Pass fell, the rebels had Geshu Han summon him to surrender; he refused, and they sent Wu Lingxun to attack.
translations.idiomatic: After Tong Pass fell, the rebels used Geshu Han to summon his surrender; he refused, and Wu Lingxun was sent to attack.

sentences.zh: 令珣死，田承嗣繼往。

translations.literal: Lingxun died; Tian Chengsi succeeded him in the attack.
translations.idiomatic: Lingxun died, and Tian Chengsi took over the assault.

sentences.zh: 潁川來瑱、襄陽魏仲犀合兵援炅。

translations.literal: Lai Tian of Yingchuan and Wei Zhongxi of Xiangyang combined forces to relieve Jiong.
translations.idiomatic: Lai Tian of Yingchuan and Wei Zhongxi of Xiangyang joined forces to relieve Jiong.

sentences.zh: 仲犀弟孟馴兵至明府橋，望賊走。

translations.literal: Zhongxi's younger brother Mengxun led troops to Mingfu Bridge, saw the rebels, and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxi's brother Mengxun reached Mingfu Bridge, sighted the rebels, and fled.

sentences.zh: 炅城中食盡，米鬥五十千，一鼠四百，餓者相枕藉。

translations.literal: Food in the city was exhausted; rice was fifty thousand per dou, a rat four hundred; the starving lay pillowed upon one another.
translations.idiomatic: Food in the city ran out; rice sold for fifty thousand cash per dou and a rat for four hundred; the starving lay piled upon one another.

sentences.zh: 朝廷遣使者曹日昇宣慰，加炅特進、太仆卿，不得入。

translations.literal: The court sent the envoy Cao Risheng to offer comfort and additionally made Jiong Specially Advanced and Minister of the Stud, but he could not enter.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent envoy Cao Risheng with condolences and promoted Jiong to Specially Advanced and Minister of the Stud, but he could not enter the city.

sentences.zh: 日昇請單騎致命，仲犀不可。

translations.literal: Risheng asked to go alone on horseback to deliver the message; Zhongxi would not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: Risheng asked to ride in alone to deliver the imperial message; Zhongxi refused.

sentences.zh: 會顏真卿自河北至，謂曰：「使者不顧死，致天子命，設為賊獲，是亡一使者；

translations.literal: When Yan Zhenqing arrived from Hebei, he said: "The envoy disregards death to deliver the Son of Heaven's command. If he is taken by rebels, that is the loss of one envoy;
translations.idiomatic: When Yan Zhenqing arrived from Hebei, he said, "The envoy is willing to risk death to deliver the emperor's orders. If the rebels capture him, we lose one envoy;

sentences.zh: 脫能入城，則萬心固矣。」

translations.literal: if he can enter the city, then ten thousand hearts will be secured."
translations.idiomatic: but if he reaches the city, every heart there will be steadied."

sentences.zh: 中官馮廷瑰亦曰：「將軍必入，我請以兩騎助。」

translations.literal: The eunuch Feng Tinggui also said: "The general must enter; I ask to assist with two horsemen."
translations.idiomatic: Eunuch Feng Tinggui added, "You must go in, General—I will send two horsemen to escort you."

sentences.zh: 仲犀益騎凡十輩。

translations.literal: Zhongxi added horsemen until there were ten in all.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxi added escorts until there were ten horsemen in all.

sentences.zh: 賊望見，知皆銳兵，不敢擊，遂入致命，人心益固。

translations.literal: The rebels saw them from afar, knew they were all elite troops, and did not dare attack; thus he entered and delivered the message, and morale grew firmer.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels saw them from afar, recognized elite troops, and did not dare attack. Risheng entered and delivered the message, and morale in the city strengthened.

sentences.zh: 日昇復以騎趨襄陽，領兵千，由音聲道運糧餉炅，故炅得與賊相持逾三月。

translations.literal: Risheng again rode swiftly to Xiangyang, led a thousand troops, and transported grain to Jiong by the Yinsheng route; thus Jiong was able to hold against the rebels for more than three months.
translations.idiomatic: Risheng rode to Xiangyang, raised a thousand men, and brought grain to Jiong along the Yinsheng route, enabling him to hold against the rebels for more than three months.

sentences.zh: 炅被圍凡一年，晝夜戰，人至相食，卒無救。

translations.literal: Jiong was besieged for a full year, fighting day and night; people came to eating one another, and in the end there was no relief.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong was besieged for a full year, fighting day and night until people ate one another; in the end no relief came.

sentences.zh: 至德二載五月，乃率眾突圍走襄陽。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the second year of Zhide, he then led his forces in a breakout toward Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Zhide year 2 he led a breakout toward Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 承嗣尾擊，炅殊死戰二日，斬獲甚眾，賊引去。

translations.literal: Chengsi pursued from behind; Jiong fought to the death for two days, beheading and capturing many; the rebels withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Chengsi pursued from behind; Jiong fought desperately for two days, killing and capturing many before the rebels withdrew.

sentences.zh: 俄拜御史大夫、襄鄧十州節度使。

translations.literal: Shortly he was appointed Censor-in-Chief and military commissioner of the ten prefectures of Xiang and Deng.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Censor-in-Chief and commissioner of the ten Xiang and Deng prefectures.

sentences.zh: 亦會二京平，賊走河北。

translations.literal: It also happened that the two capitals were pacified and the rebels fled to Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: By then both capitals had been recovered and the rebels had fled to Hebei.

sentences.zh: 時襄、漢數百里，鄉聚蕩然，舉無樵煙。

translations.literal: At the time, for several hundred li in Xiang and Han, villages and hamlets were laid waste; nowhere was there smoke from woodcutters.
translations.idiomatic: For hundreds of li around Xiang and Han, villages lay in ruins and not a wisp of hearth smoke could be seen.

sentences.zh: 初，賊欲剽亂江湖，賴炅適扼其沖，故南夏以完。

translations.literal: Earlier the rebels had wished to plunder and throw the riverlands into chaos; it was because Jiong happened to block their vital point that southern Xia was preserved intact.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels had planned to ravage the Yangzi region; Jiong happened to block their path, and so the south was spared.

sentences.zh: 策勛封岐國公，實封二百戶。

translations.literal: For recorded merit he was enfeoffed as Duke of Qi, with a substantive fief of two hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was enfeoffed as Duke of Qi with an income of two hundred households.

sentences.zh: 乾元元年，又加淮西節度、鄧州刺史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianyuan he was additionally made military commissioner of Huaixi and prefect of Deng.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qianyuan he was also made military commissioner of Huaixi and prefect of Deng.

sentences.zh: 與九節度圍安慶緒於相州，炅領淮西、襄陽兩鎮步卒萬人、騎三百。

translations.literal: With the nine commissioners he besieged An Qingxu at Xiangzhou; Jiong led ten thousand infantry of the Huai and Xiang commands and three hundred horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: With the nine commissioners he besieged An Qingxu at Xiangzhou. Jiong commanded ten thousand foot soldiers from the Huai and Xiang commands and three hundred horsemen.

sentences.zh: 明年，與史思明戰安陽，王師不利，炅中流矢，輒奔，諸節度潰去，所過剽奪，而炅軍尤甚。

translations.literal: The next year he fought Shi Siming at Anyang; the imperial army fared poorly. Jiong was struck by an arrow and fled at once. The commissioners broke and fled, plundering wherever they passed, and Jiong's army was worst of all.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he fought Shi Siming at Anyang. The imperial army was defeated, Jiong was wounded by an arrow and fled, and the commissioners broke and scattered, plundering as they went—Jiong's troops worst of all.

sentences.zh: 有詔來瑱節度淮西，徙炅鄭陳亳節度使。

translations.literal: An edict made Lai Tian military commissioner of Huaixi and transferred Jiong to be military commissioner of Zheng, Chen, and Bo.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made Lai Tian commissioner of Huaixi and transferred Jiong to the Zheng-Chen-Bo command.

sentences.zh: 至新鄭，聞郭子儀整軍屯谷水，李光弼還太原，炅羞惴，仰藥死，年五十七。

translations.literal: Reaching Xinzheng, he heard that Guo Ziyi had reorganized his army and garrisoned Gushui and that Li Guangbi had returned to Taiyuan. Ashamed and fearful, Jiong took poison and died at fifty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: At Xinzheng he learned that Guo Ziyi had reorganized his army at Gushui and that Li Guangbi had returned to Taiyuan. Ashamed and afraid, Jiong took poison and died at fifty-seven.

sentences.zh: 王難得，沂州臨沂人。

translations.literal: Wang Nande was a native of Linyi in Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Nande was from Linyi in Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 父思敬，少隸軍，試太子賓客。

translations.literal: His father Sijing entered the army in youth and was appointed acting Guest of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: His father Sijing entered the army young and rose to acting Guest of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 難得健於武，工騎射。

translations.literal: Nande was strong in martial arts and skilled in mounted archery.
translations.idiomatic: Nande was powerfully built and expert in mounted archery.

sentences.zh: 天寶初，為河源軍使。

translations.literal: In the early Tianbao era he was made commander of the Heyuan Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Tianbao period he became commander of the Heyuan Army.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃贊普子郎支都者，恃趫敏，乘名馬，寶鈿鞍，略陣挑戰，甚閑暇，無敢校者。

translations.literal: The Tibetan emperor's son Langzhidu relied on his swift agility, rode a famous horse with a jeweled saddle, skirmished before the lines to challenge battle, very much at ease, and none dared contend with him.
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetan prince Langzhidu, relying on his speed and agility, rode a famous horse with a jeweled saddle and challenged the lines at leisure; no one dared face him.

sentences.zh: 難得怒，挾矛駷馬馳，支都不暇鬥，直斬其首。

translations.literal: Nande grew angry, grasped his spear and galloped; Langzhidu had no leisure to fight and was beheaded outright.
translations.idiomatic: Nande flew into a rage, seized his spear, and charged; Langzhidu had no time to fight back and was beheaded on the spot.

sentences.zh: 玄宗壯其果，召見，令殿前乘馬挾矛作刺賊狀，大悅，賜錦袍、金帶。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong admired his boldness, summoned him, and had him before the hall mount a horse, grasp a spear, and perform the posture of thrusting at rebels. Greatly pleased, he bestowed a brocade robe and gold belt.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong admired his daring, summoned him, and had him demonstrate spear thrusts against imaginary rebels from horseback before the hall. Delighted, the emperor gave him a brocade robe and gold belt.

sentences.zh: 累授金吾將軍。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly appointed General of the Gold Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through repeated appointments to General of the Gold Guard.

sentences.zh: 從哥舒翰擊吐蕃，至積石，虜吐谷渾王子悉弄參及悉頰藏而還。

translations.literal: He followed Geshu Han in striking Tibet, reaching Jishi, capturing the Tuyuhun princes Sinongcan and Siniangzang, and returning.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Geshu Han against Tibet to Jishi, captured the Tuyuhun princes Sinongcan and Siniangzang, and returned.

sentences.zh: 復收五橋，拔樹惇城，進白水軍使。

translations.literal: He again recovered the Five Bridges, captured Shudun City, and was advanced to commander of the Baishui Army.
translations.idiomatic: He recovered the Five Bridges, took Shudun City, and was promoted to commander of the Baishui Army.

sentences.zh: 收九曲，加特進。

translations.literal: In recovering Jiuqu he was made Specially Advanced.
translations.idiomatic: For recovering Jiuqu he was made Specially Advanced.

sentences.zh: 肅宗在靈武，軍賞乏，難得上家貲助軍，試衛尉卿。

translations.literal: When Emperor Suzong was at Lingwu, military rewards were scarce; Nande contributed his family's wealth to aid the army and was appointed acting Minister of the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Suzong was at Lingwu and military funds ran short, Nande contributed his family wealth to the army and was made acting Minister of the Guard.

sentences.zh: 俄領興平軍及鳳翔兵馬使，收京師。

translations.literal: Soon he led the Xingping Army and was military commissioner of Fengxiang troops in recovering the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He soon commanded the Xingping Army and Fengxiang forces in the recovery of the capital.

sentences.zh: 方戰，麾下士失馬，難得馳救，矢著眉，披膚鄣目，乃拔箭斷膚，殊死前鬥，血蔑面不已，帝嘉之。

translations.literal: In battle a soldier under his command lost his horse; Nande galloped to rescue him. An arrow struck his brow; he tore skin to cover his eyes, then pulled out the arrow and cut away the flesh, fought desperately forward, blood covering his face without cease. The emperor praised him.
translations.idiomatic: In battle a subordinate lost his horse; Nande charged to save him. An arrow struck his brow; he tore skin to shield his eyes, pulled out the arrow and cut away the flesh, and fought on desperately, his face streaming with blood. The emperor praised his valor.

sentences.zh: 從郭子儀攻相州。

translations.literal: He followed Guo Ziyi in attacking Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Guo Ziyi in the attack on Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 累封瑯邪郡公，為英武軍使。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly enfeoffed as Duke of Langye and made commander of the Yingwu Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Duke of Langye and made commander of the Yingwu Army.

sentences.zh: 寶應二年，卒，贈潞州大都督。

translations.literal: In the second year of Baoying he died and was posthumously made Grand Protector of Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Baoying year 2 and was posthumously made Grand Protector of Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 子子顏，少從父征討，檢校衛尉卿，生莊憲太后。

translations.literal: His son Ziyan, in youth following his father on campaigns, was made acting Minister of the Guard and fathered Empress Dowager Zhuangxian.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ziyan followed his father on campaigns from youth, rose to acting Minister of the Guard, and fathered Empress Dowager Zhuangxian.

sentences.zh: 元和元年，憲宗朝太后南宮，乃褒贈思敬為司徒，難得太尉，子顏太師。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanhe, when Emperor Xianzong attended the empress dowager at the Southern Palace, he posthumously honored Sijing as Minister of Works, made Nande Grand Marshal, and Ziyan Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanhe year 1, when Xianzong attended the empress dowager at the Southern Palace, he posthumously honored Sijing as Minister of Works, made Nande Grand Marshal, and Ziyan Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 唯子顏子用及封。

translations.literal: Only Ziyan's son Yong and enfeoffments follow.
translations.idiomatic: Only Ziyan's son Yong and his enfeoffments follow.

sentences.zh: 用字師柔。

translations.literal: Yong was styled Shirou.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yong was styled Shirou.

sentences.zh: 拜太子詹事，才三月，封太原郡公，掌廄苑。

translations.literal: He was appointed Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent; after only three months he was enfeoffed as Duke of Taiyuan and placed in charge of the imperial stables and parks.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent; after only three months he was enfeoffed as Duke of Taiyuan and put in charge of the imperial stables and parks.

sentences.zh: 累遷檢校左散騎常侍，兼右金吾大將軍。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly transferred to Acting Left Regular Attendant and concurrently Grand General of the Right Gold Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Acting Left Regular Attendant and concurrently Grand General of the Right Gold Guard.

sentences.zh: 謙畏無過。

translations.literal: He was modest and cautious and committed no faults.
translations.idiomatic: Modest and cautious, he committed no fault.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈工部尚書。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 辛雲京，蘭州金城人，客籍京兆，世為將家。

translations.literal: Xin Yunjing was a native of Jincheng in Lanzhou, registered as a guest in Jingzhao; for generations his family had been military men.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Yunjing was from Jincheng in Lanzhou but registered in Jingzhao; his family had been soldiers for generations.

sentences.zh: 雲京有膽決，以禽生斬馘常冠軍，積功遷特進、太常卿。

translations.literal: Yunjing had bold resolve; through capturing enemies alive, beheading them, and taking heads he often led the army in victory. For accumulated merit he was transferred to Specially Advanced and Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: Yunjing was bold and decisive; his captures, beheadings, and trophies often led the army, and for accumulated merit he rose to Specially Advanced and Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 史思明屯相州，雲京以銳兵四千襲滏陽，追破其眾，至浪井。

translations.literal: When Shi Siming encamped at Xiangzhou, Yunjing with four thousand elite troops raided Fuyang, pursued and routed his forces, and reached Langjing.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Siming held Xiangzhou, Yunjing struck Fuyang with four thousand elite troops, routed his force in pursuit, and reached Langjing.

sentences.zh: 錄多，授開府儀同三司，加代州都督、鎮北兵馬使。

translations.literal: His recorded merits were many; he was appointed Grand Master with the same privileges as the Three Excellencies and additionally made Protector-General of Daizhou and northern frontier military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: For his many recorded victories he was made Grand Master with privileges equal to the Three Excellencies and also Protector-General of Daizhou and northern frontier military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 太原軍亂，帝惡鄧景山繩下無漸，以雲京性沈毅，故授太原尹，進封金城郡王。

translations.literal: When the Taiyuan army mutinied, the emperor disliked Deng Jingshan's lack of gradual discipline over subordinates; because Yunjing's nature was deep and resolute, he was appointed mayor of Taiyuan and advanced to Prince of Jincheng commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When the Taiyuan army mutinied, the emperor blamed Deng Jingshan for ruling too harshly without gradual discipline and, trusting Yunjing's steady resolve, made him mayor of Taiyuan and Prince of Jincheng.

sentences.zh: 雲京治謹於法，下有犯，雖絲毫比不肯貸，及賞功亦如之，故軍中畏而信。

translations.literal: Yunjing governed with strict adherence to law; when subordinates offended, even the slightest comparison he would not pardon, and in rewarding merit he was likewise exact, so the army both feared and trusted him.
translations.idiomatic: Yunjing ruled with strict discipline; the smallest offense went unpunished, and rewards were meted out with equal exactness, so his troops both feared and trusted him.

sentences.zh: 回紇恃舊勛，每入朝，所在暴鈔，至太原，雲京以戎狄待之，虜畏不敢惕息。

translations.literal: The Uyghurs relied on old merit; whenever they came to court they plundered wherever they went. At Taiyuan, Yunjing treated them as barbarians; the tribesmen feared him and did not dare breathe freely.
translations.idiomatic: The Uyghurs, relying on past service, plundered wherever they went on court visits. At Taiyuan Yunjing treated them as barbarians, and they were too afraid even to breathe freely.

sentences.zh: 數年，太原大治。

translations.literal: Within several years Taiyuan was greatly well governed.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years Taiyuan was thoroughly pacified and prospered.

sentences.zh: 加檢校尚書右仆射、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: He was additionally made Acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Associate Grand Councilor of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Acting Right Vice Director of State Affairs and Associate Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 大歷三年，檢校左仆射。

translations.literal: In the third year of Dali he was Acting Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: In Dali year 3 he became Acting Left Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 卒，年五十五，代宗為發哀流涕，贈太尉，謚曰忠獻。

translations.literal: He died at fifty-five; Emperor Daizong wept at his mourning; he was posthumously made Grand Preceptor with the posthumous title Loyal and Offering.
translations.idiomatic: He died at fifty-five. Daizong wept at his passing and posthumously made him Grand Preceptor with the title Loyal and Offering.

sentences.zh: 它日，郭子儀、元載見上，語及雲京，帝必泫然。

translations.literal: On other days when Guo Ziyi and Yuan Zai saw the emperor and spoke of Yunjing, he would always be tearful.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Guo Ziyi or Yuan Zai mentioned Yunjing to the emperor, he would tear up.

sentences.zh: 及葬，命中使吊祠，時將相祭者至七十餘幄，喪車移晷乃得去。

translations.literal: At the burial he ordered palace envoys to offer sacrifices; at the time generals and ministers making offerings reached more than seventy canopies; the funeral procession moved for a full day before it could depart.
translations.idiomatic: At his burial the emperor sent palace envoys to offer sacrifices; more than seventy generals and ministers attended, and the funeral procession took a full day to pass.

sentences.zh: 德宗時，第至德以來將相，雲京為次。

translations.literal: In Emperor Dezong's time, when ranking generals and ministers since Zhide, Yunjing was second.
translations.idiomatic: Under Dezong, among generals and ministers since the Zhide era, Yunjing ranked second.

sentences.zh: 從弟京杲，字京杲。

translations.literal: His younger cousin Jinggao was styled Jinggao.
translations.idiomatic: His cousin Jinggao was also styled Jinggao.

sentences.zh: 信安王祎節度朔方，京杲與弟旻以策幹說，祎評咨加異。

translations.literal: When Prince Xin'an Li Yi held Shuofang, Jinggao and his younger brother Min presented stratagems to persuade him; Yi evaluated them with special regard.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Xin'an Li Yi commanded Shuofang, Jinggao and his brother Min presented plans that Yi received with special favor.

sentences.zh: 後從李光弼出井陘，督趫蕩先驅，戰嘉山尤力，肅宗異之，召見曰：「黥、彭、關、張之流乎！」

translations.literal: Later he followed Li Guangbi out through Jingxing Pass, directed swift raiders as vanguard, fought with especial force at Jia Mountain. Emperor Suzong was struck by him and summoned him, saying: "A man of the stripe of Qing Bu, Peng Yue, Guan Yu, and Zhang Fei!"
translations.idiomatic: Later he followed Li Guangbi through Jingxing Pass, led swift raiders as vanguard, and fought fiercely at Jia Mountain. Suzong was impressed, summoned him, and exclaimed, "A man in the mold of Qing Bu, Peng Yue, Guan Yu, and Zhang Fei!"

sentences.zh: 累遷鴻臚卿，召為英武軍使。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly transferred to Minister of the Court for Dependencies and summoned as commander of the Yingwu Army.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Minister of the Court for Dependencies and was summoned as commander of the Yingwu Army.

sentences.zh: 代宗立，封肅國公，遷左金吾衛大將軍，進晉昌郡王，歷湖南觀察使，後為工部尚書致仕。

translations.literal: When Emperor Daizong ascended, he was enfeoffed as Duke of Suguo, transferred to Grand General of the Left Gold Guard, advanced to Prince of Jinchang commandery, served as observation commissioner of Hunan, and later retired as Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: When Daizong ascended, he was enfeoffed Duke of Suguo, made Grand General of the Left Gold Guard, advanced to Prince of Jinchang, served as Hunan observation commissioner, and later retired as Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 朱泚盜京師，以老病不能從，西向慟而卒，贈太子少保。

translations.literal: When Zhu Ci seized the capital, because of old age and illness he could not follow; he faced west, wailed, and died; he was posthumously made Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Ci seized the capital, age and illness kept him from following; he faced west, wailed, and died, and was posthumously made Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 旻亦從光弼定恒、趙，後署太原三城使。

translations.literal: Min also followed Guangbi in pacifying Heng and Zhao, and was later appointed commissioner of the three cities of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Min also followed Guangbi in pacifying Heng and Zhao and was later made commissioner of Taiyuan's three cities.

sentences.zh: 史思明屯相，軍及滏陽，旻逆擊走之。

translations.literal: When Shi Siming encamped at Xiang, his army reached Fuyang; Min met and drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Siming held Xiang and his army reached Fuyang, Min met them and drove them off.

sentences.zh: 東都陷，退守河陽，卒於屯。

translations.literal: When the Eastern Capital fell, he withdrew to defend Heyang and died in camp.
translations.idiomatic: When the Eastern Capital fell, he withdrew to Heyang and died in camp.

sentences.zh: 雲京曾孫讜，別傳。

translations.literal: Yunjing's great-grandson Dan has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: Yunjing's great-grandson Dan is treated in a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 馮河清，京兆人。

translations.literal: Feng Heqing was a native of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Heqing was from Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 始隸郭子儀軍，以戰多拜左衛大將軍。

translations.literal: He first served in Guo Ziyi's army; for many battles he was appointed Grand General of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He first served under Guo Ziyi and, for many battles, was made Grand General of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 後從涇原節度使馬璘，充兵馬使，數以偏師與吐蕃遇，多效級，名聞軍中。

translations.literal: Later he followed Jingyuan commissioner Ma Lin as military commissioner, often met Tibet with detached forces, frequently presented heads, and his name was known throughout the army.
translations.idiomatic: He later served Jingyuan commissioner Ma Lin as military commander, often met Tibetans with detached forces, frequently presented trophies, and became famous in the army.

sentences.zh: 建中時，節度使姚令言率兵討關東，以河清知留後，幕府殿中侍御史姚況領州；

translations.literal: In the Jianzhong era, commissioner Yao Lingyan led troops to pacify the east and left Heqing as acting commissioner; the staff Palace Attendant Yao Kuang held the prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: During Jianzhong, commissioner Yao Lingyan led troops to pacify the east, leaving Heqing as acting commissioner while staff member Yao Kuang, a Palace Attendant, held the prefecture;

sentences.zh: 而行師過闕，有急變，德宗走奉天。

translations.literal: but as the marching army passed the capital there was a sudden crisis and Emperor Dezong fled to Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: but as the army marched past the capital a sudden crisis erupted and Emperor Dezong fled to Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 河清、況聞問，召諸將計事，東向哭，相勵以忠，意象軒毅，眾義其為，無敢異言，即發儲鎧完仗百餘乘獻行在。

translations.literal: Heqing and Kuang heard the news, summoned the generals to plan, wept facing east, and encouraged one another with loyalty; their bearing was lofty and stern; the crowd approved their conduct and none dared dissent; they immediately sent out more than a hundred cartloads of stored armor and complete weapons to the imperial camp.
translations.idiomatic: Heqing and Kuang heard the news, summoned the generals to plan, wept facing east, and urged one another to loyalty; their bearing was lofty and resolute; the men approved their conduct and none dared dissent; they immediately dispatched more than a hundred cartloads of stored armor and complete weapons to the imperial camp.

sentences.zh: 初，帝之出，六軍倉卒無良兵，士氣沮。

translations.literal: At first when the emperor fled, the Six Armies in haste had no good troops and morale was crushed.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor first fled, the Six Armies in their haste had no reliable troops and morale collapsed.

sentences.zh: 及河清輸械至，被堅勒兵，軍聲大振。

translations.literal: When Heqing's weapons arrived, they donned armor and tightened ranks; the army's spirit greatly revived.
translations.idiomatic: When Heqing's weapons arrived, the troops donned armor and tightened ranks, and the army's spirit surged.

sentences.zh: 即拜河清涇原節度使、安定郡王，況行軍司馬。

translations.literal: Heqing was immediately appointed Jingyuan commissioner and Prince of Anding; Kuang became field army marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Heqing was immediately appointed Jingyuan commissioner and Prince of Anding; Kuang was made field army marshal.

sentences.zh: 朱泚數遣諜人訹之，河清輒斬以徇。

translations.literal: Zhu Ci repeatedly sent spies to entice him; Heqing would execute them and display the bodies.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ci repeatedly sent spies to win him over; Heqing would execute them and display the bodies.

sentences.zh: 興元元年，渾瑊以吐蕃兵敗賊韓旻等，涇人妄傳吐蕃有功，將以叛卒孥與貲歸之，眾大恐，且言：「不殺馮公，吾等無類矣。」

translations.literal: In the first year of Xingyuan, Hun Jian defeated the rebel Han Min and others with Tibetan troops; the people of Jing falsely spread that Tibet had merit and would take the rebel soldiers' wives, children, and goods back to them; the crowd was greatly afraid and said: "If we do not kill Lord Feng, we shall have no survivors."
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xingyuan, Hun Jian defeated rebel Han Min with Tibetan troops. The people of Jing falsely claimed Tibet deserved credit and would take rebel families and goods; panic spread, and they said, "Unless we kill Lord Feng, none of us will survive."

sentences.zh: 田希鑒遂害河清，況挺身還鄉里。

translations.literal: Tian Xijian then killed Heqing; Kuang made his way alone back to his home district.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Xijian then murdered Heqing; Kuang escaped alone to his home district.

sentences.zh: 京師平，贈河清尚書左仆射，拜況太子中舍人。

translations.literal: When the capital was pacified, Heqing was posthumously made Left Vice Director; Kuang was appointed Palace Attendant of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital was recovered, Heqing was posthumously made Left Vice Director and Kuang was appointed Attendant of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 況性簡退，未嘗言功，屬歲兇，奉稍不自給，以饑死。

translations.literal: Kuang's nature was simple and retiring; he never spoke of merit; in years of famine his salary could not support him and he died of hunger.
translations.idiomatic: Kuang was modest and retiring and never spoke of his deeds; in famine years his salary could not sustain him, and he starved to death.

sentences.zh: 河清再贈太子少傅。

translations.literal: Heqing was again posthumously made Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Heqing received a second posthumous promotion to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 李芃，字茂初，趙州人。

translations.literal: Li Peng was styled Maochu, a native of Zhao prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Peng, styled Maochu, was a native of Zhao prefecture.

sentences.zh: 解褐上邽主簿。

translations.literal: Upon leaving the russet he was appointed chief clerk of Shanggui.
translations.idiomatic: Upon entering official service he was appointed chief clerk of Shanggui.

sentences.zh: 嚴武為京兆尹，薦補長安尉。

translations.literal: When Yan Wu was mayor of Jingzhao, he recommended him to fill the post of bailiff of Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan Wu was mayor of Jingzhao, he recommended Peng to fill the post of bailiff of Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 李勉觀察江西，表署判官。

translations.literal: When Li Mian was observation commissioner of Jiangxi, he memorialized appointing him as aide.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Mian was observation commissioner of Jiangxi, he memorialized appointing Peng as aide.

sentences.zh: 永泰初，宣饒劇賊方清、陳莊西絕江，劫商旅為亂，支黨槃結。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongtai, the fierce bandits Fang Qing and Chen Zhuang of Xuan and Rao cut off the west bank of the river, plundered merchants and travelers into disorder, and their branches were tightly knotted.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yongtai, the fierce bandits Fang Qing and Chen Zhuang of Xuan and Rao cut off the west bank of the river, plundered merchants and travelers, and their network was tightly knit.

sentences.zh: 芃請以秋浦置州，扼衿要，使不得合從。

translations.literal: Peng asked to establish a prefecture at Qiupu to choke the vital point so they could not unite.
translations.idiomatic: Peng proposed establishing a prefecture at Qiupu to hold the strategic chokepoint and prevent them from joining forces.

sentences.zh: 勉是其計，奏以宣之秋浦青陽、饒之至德置池州。

translations.literal: Mian approved his plan and memorialized to take Qiupu and Qingyang of Xuan and Zhide of Rao to establish Chizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Mian approved the plan and memorialized to establish Chizhou from Qiupu and Qingyang of Xuan and Zhide of Rao.

sentences.zh: 即詔芃行州事。

translations.literal: He was immediately ordered to administer the prefecture's affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Peng was immediately ordered to administer the prefecture's affairs.

sentences.zh: 後魏少遊代勉，表署都團練副使，攝江州刺史。

translations.literal: Later Wei Shaoyou replaced Mian and memorialized appointing him deputy regimental training commissioner, acting prefect of Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: Later Wei Shaoyou replaced Mian and memorialized appointing Peng deputy regimental training commissioner and acting prefect of Jiang.

sentences.zh: 以母喪解。

translations.literal: He resigned on his mother's death.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 勉之節度永平，復辟幕府。

translations.literal: When Mian held Yongping, he again recruited him to his staff.
translations.idiomatic: When Mian held Yongping, he again recruited Peng to his staff.

sentences.zh: 會李靈耀反，署芃兼亳州防禦使，護陳、潁饟道，便軍興。

translations.literal: When Li Lingyao rebelled, he appointed Peng concurrently defense commissioner of Bozhou, protecting the grain routes of Chen and Ying, facilitating military mobilization.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Lingyao rebelled, Mian appointed Peng concurrently defense commissioner of Bozhou, protecting the grain routes of Chen and Ying to facilitate military mobilization.

sentences.zh: 德宗立，授河陽三城鎮遏使。

translations.literal: When Emperor Dezong ascended, he was made suppressor of the three cities of Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Dezong ascended, Peng was made suppressor of the three cities of Heyang.

sentences.zh: 糧貲善者，必先以給士，士悅之。

translations.literal: When grain and goods were good, he always gave to the soldiers first; the soldiers were pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever supplies were plentiful, he always distributed them to the soldiers first; the troops were pleased.

sentences.zh: 達練事宜，嚴備常若有敵。

translations.literal: He understood military affairs thoroughly and maintained strict readiness as though enemies were always present.
translations.idiomatic: Thoroughly versed in military affairs, he maintained strict readiness as though enemies were always at hand.

sentences.zh: 未幾，拜節度使，以東畿汜水等五縣隸屬。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed military commissioner, with five counties including Si River of the eastern capital placed under him.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed military commissioner, with five counties including Si River of the eastern capital placed under his jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 與馬燧等破田悅洹水上，以功檢校兵部尚書，實封百戶。

translations.literal: With Ma Sui and others he defeated Tian Yue on the Huan River; for merit he was made Acting Minister of War with a substantive fief of one hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: With Ma Sui and others he defeated Tian Yue on the Huan River and was made Acting Minister of War with an income of one hundred households.

sentences.zh: 進圍悅，悅將符璘以騎五百降，芃大開壁門納之。

translations.literal: Advancing to besiege Yue, Yue's general Fu Lin surrendered with five hundred horsemen; Peng opened the barricade gate wide to receive them.
translations.idiomatic: Pressing the siege, Yue's general Fu Lin surrendered with five hundred cavalry; Peng threw open the gate to welcome them.

sentences.zh: 興元初，檢校尚書右仆射。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xingyuan he was Acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xingyuan era he became Acting Right Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 以疾將請老，謂所親曰：「歲方旱蝗，上厭征伐，天下城壘堅，戈鋋利，然務以力勝，其可盡乎？

translations.literal: Ill and about to request retirement, he said to those close to him: "The year is afflicted with drought and locusts; the emperor is weary of campaigns; fortresses throughout the realm are strong and blades sharp—yet they insist on victory by force alone. Can this be exhausted?
translations.idiomatic: As illness drove him to seek retirement, he told his intimates, "Drought and locusts afflict the land, the emperor is weary of war, and though every fortress is strong and every blade sharp, they still insist on winning by force alone. Can that go on forever?

sentences.zh: 救敝者莫若德，方鎮之臣宜先退讓，死權錮祿，吾敢哉！

translations.literal: To rescue exhaustion nothing is better than virtue; frontier commissioners ought first to yield; to die clutching power and fettered salary—would I dare?
translations.idiomatic: Virtue, not force, is how to heal exhaustion; frontier lords should yield first. To die clutching office and salary—would I dare do that?

sentences.zh: 言而不踐，非吾誌也。」

translations.literal: To speak and not act is not my intent.
translations.idiomatic: Words without deeds are not my way."

sentences.zh: 固求罷，歸東都。

translations.literal: He firmly sought dismissal and returned to the eastern capital.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed hard for release and retired to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十四，贈太子太保。

translations.literal: He died at sixty-four and was posthumously made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-four and was posthumously honored as Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 李叔明，字晉，閬州新政人。

translations.literal: Li Shuming was styled Jin, a native of Xinzheng in Lang prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shuming, styled Jin, was from Xinzheng in Langzhou.

sentences.zh: 本鮮于氏，世為右族。

translations.literal: Originally of the Xianyu clan, for generations a great house on the right.
translations.idiomatic: His family was originally the Xianyu clan, a great house for generations.

sentences.zh: 兄仲通，字向，天寶末為京兆尹、劍南節度使。

translations.literal: His elder brother Zhongtong was styled Xiang; at the end of Tianbao he was mayor of Jingzhao and military commissioner of Jiannan.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Zhongtong, styled Xiang, was mayor of Jingzhao and Jiannan commissioner at the end of Tianbao.

sentences.zh: 兄弟皆涉學，輕財務施。

translations.literal: The brothers all studied, were light with wealth and devoted to giving.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers were educated, generous with wealth, and devoted to charity.

sentences.zh: 叔明擢明經，為楊國忠劍南判官。

translations.literal: Shuming passed the Mingjing examination and was Yang Guozhong's Jiannan aide.
translations.idiomatic: Shuming passed the Mingjing examination and served as Yang Guozhong's Jiannan aide.

sentences.zh: 乾元中，除司勛員外郎，副漢中王瑀使回紇，回紇遇瑀慢，叔明讓曰：「大國通好，使賢王持節。

translations.literal: In Qianyuan he was made Vice Director of Merits and deputy to Prince of Hanzhong Li Yu on mission to the Uyghurs; the Uyghurs treated Yu with disrespect; Shuming reproved them: "Great states are on friendly terms; an illustrious prince bears the credentials.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianyuan he was Vice Director of Merits and accompanied Prince of Hanzhong Li Yu to the Uyghurs; when they treated Yu disrespectfully, Shuming rebuked them: "Great states are allies; an illustrious prince bears the imperial credentials.

sentences.zh: 可汗，唐之婿，恃功而倨，可乎？」

translations.literal: Khan, you are the Tang emperor's son-in-law—relying on merit and acting arrogantly—is that permissible?"
translations.idiomatic: Khan, you are the Tang emperor's son-in-law—will you rely on past merit and act arrogantly?"

sentences.zh: 可汗為加禮。

translations.literal: The khan therefore treated him with added ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: The khan then treated them with added ceremony.

sentences.zh: 復命，遷司門郎中。

translations.literal: On his return he was transferred to Director of the Gate Office.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was made Director of the Gate Office.

sentences.zh: 東都平，拜洛陽令，招徠遺民，號能吏。

translations.literal: When the Eastern Capital was pacified, he was appointed magistrate of Luoyang, recruited scattered people, and was called a capable official.
translations.idiomatic: When the Eastern Capital was recovered he was made magistrate of Luoyang, recruited the scattered populace, and was hailed as a capable official.

sentences.zh: 擢商州刺史、上津轉運使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to prefect of Shang and transport commissioner of Shangjin.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to prefect of Shang and made transport commissioner of Shangjin.

sentences.zh: 遷京兆尹，長安歌曰：「前尹赫赫，具瞻允若；

translations.literal: He was transferred to mayor of Jingzhao; Chang'an sang: "The former mayor was illustrious, all looked up and approved;
translations.idiomatic: Made mayor of Jingzhao, Chang'an sang, "The former mayor was illustrious, and all looked up in approval;

sentences.zh: 後尹熙熙，具瞻允斯。」

translations.literal: the later mayor is harmonious, all look up and approve thus."
translations.idiomatic: the later mayor is gracious, and all look up in the same way."

sentences.zh: 久之，以疾辭，除太子右庶子。

translations.literal: After long service he resigned on illness and was made Right Companion of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: After long service he resigned on grounds of illness and was made Right Companion of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 崔旰擾成都，出為卬州刺史。

translations.literal: When Cui Gan disturbed Chengdu, he was sent out as prefect of Qiong.
translations.idiomatic: When Cui Gan troubled Chengdu, he was sent out as prefect of Qiong.

sentences.zh: 旰入朝，即拜東川節度使、遂州刺史，徙治梓州。

translations.literal: When Gan entered court, Shuming was immediately made commissioner of eastern Chuan and prefect of Suizhou, moving his seat to Zizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Gan came to court, Shuming was immediately made eastern Chuan commissioner and prefect of Suizhou, with his seat at Zizhou.

sentences.zh: 大歷末，或言叔明本嚴氏，少孤，養外家，冒鮮于姓，請還宗。

translations.literal: At the end of Dali someone said Shuming was originally of the Yan clan, orphaned young, raised by his mother's family, and had falsely taken the Xianyu surname, requesting restoration to his clan.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Dali someone said Shuming was originally of the Yan clan, orphaned young and raised by his mother's family, and had wrongly borne the Xianyu surname; he petitioned to restore his clan.

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: An edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved it.

sentences.zh: 叔明初不知，意鬼之，表乞宗姓，列屬籍，代宗從之。

translations.literal: Shuming at first did not know, thought it supernatural, memorialized to beg his clan surname, be entered in the clan registers; Daizong consented.
translations.idiomatic: Shuming had not known this at first and thought it supernatural; he memorialized to recover his clan name and be entered in the registers, and Daizong agreed.

sentences.zh: 建中初，吐蕃襲火井，掠龍州，陷扶、文、遠三州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianzhong Tibet raided Huojing, plundered Long prefecture, and captured Fu, Wen, and Yuan prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jianzhong Tibet raided Huojing, plundered Longzhou, and captured Fu, Wen, and Yuan prefectures.

sentences.zh: 叔明分五將邀擊，走之，以功加檢校戶部尚書。

translations.literal: Shuming divided five generals to intercept and drive them off; for merit he was additionally made Acting Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Shuming sent five generals to intercept and drive them off and was made Acting Minister of Revenue for his merit.

sentences.zh: 梁崇義阻命，詔引兵下峽，戰荊門，敗其眾，襄州平，遷檢校尚書左仆射。

translations.literal: Liang Chongyi resisted orders; he was ordered to lead troops down the gorges, fought at Jingmen, defeated his forces, pacified Xiang prefecture, and was transferred to Acting Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang Chongyi defied orders, Shuming was ordered down the gorges, defeated him at Jingmen, pacified Xiangzhou, and was made Acting Left Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 德宗幸興元，出家貲助軍，悉衣幣獻宮掖，加太子太傅，封薊國公。

translations.literal: When Dezong visited Xingyuan, he contributed family wealth to aid the army, presented all robes and goods to the palace, was made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, and enfeoffed as Duke of Ji.
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong went to Xingyuan, Shuming contributed family wealth to the army, presented all robes and goods to the palace, was made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, and enfeoffed Duke of Ji.

sentences.zh: 初，東川承兵盜，鄉邑雕破，叔明治之二十年，撫接有方，華裔遂安。

translations.literal: At first eastern Chuan had suffered military banditry and villages were ruined; Shuming governed twenty years with skillful comfort and settlement, and the Chinese and foreign peoples were secure.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Chuan had suffered war and banditry and its towns were ruined; Shuming governed twenty years with skillful care until Chinese and tribal peoples were secure.

sentences.zh: 後朝京師，以病足，賜錦輦，令宦士肩舁以見，拜尚書右仆射。

translations.literal: Later he attended court at the capital; because of illness in his feet he was given a brocade palanquin and ordered eunuch attendants to carry him on their shoulders to audience; he was appointed Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: Later he came to the capital; because his feet were afflicted he was given a brocade palanquin and carried in by eunuchs for audience, and was made Right Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 乞骸骨，改太子太傅致仕。

translations.literal: He begged to retire on account of old bones and was changed to Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent in retirement.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned to retire and was made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent in retirement.

sentences.zh: 貞元三年，卒，謚曰襄。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenyuan he died; his posthumous title was Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Zhenyuan year 3; his posthumous title was Xiang.

sentences.zh: 始，叔明與仲通俱尹京兆，及兼秩御史中丞，並節制劍南，又與子昇俱兼大夫，蜀人推為盛門。

translations.literal: At first Shuming and Zhongtong both served as mayors of Jingzhao; when they concurrently held the rank of Censor-in-Chief and both controlled Jiannan, and again when Shuming and his son Sheng both held Grand Master rank, the people of Shu esteemed them as a flourishing house.
translations.idiomatic: Shuming and Zhongtong had both been mayors of Jingzhao; when they concurrently held the rank of Censor-in-Chief and both controlled Jiannan, and when Shuming and his son Sheng both held Grand Master rank, the people of Shu esteemed them as a great house.

sentences.zh: 叔明素惡道、佛之弊，上言曰：「佛，空寂無為者也；

translations.literal: Shuming had long hated the abuses of Daoism and Buddhism and memorialized: "Buddhism is empty stillness and non-action;
translations.idiomatic: Shuming had long hated the abuses of Buddhism and Daoism and memorialized: "Buddhism teaches empty stillness and non-action;

sentences.zh: 道，清虛寡欲者也。

translations.literal: Daoism is pure emptiness and few desires.
translations.idiomatic: Daoism teaches purity, emptiness, and few desires.

sentences.zh: 今迷其內而飾其外，使農夫工女墮業以避役，故農桑不勸，兵賦日屈，國用軍儲為斁耗。

translations.literal: Now they are lost within and adorn without, causing farmers and craftswomen to abandon their trades to avoid corvée; thus agriculture and sericulture are not encouraged, military levies daily shrink, and state revenue and army stores are wasted away.
translations.idiomatic: Yet people are lost within and ornate without, so farmers and craftswomen abandon their trades to avoid corvée; agriculture falters, levies shrink, and state and army stores are drained.

sentences.zh: 臣請本道定寺為三等，觀為二等，上寺留僧二十一，上觀道士十四，每等降殺以七，皆擇有行者，餘還為民。」

translations.literal: Your servant asks to fix monasteries in this circuit in three grades and abbeys in two; upper monasteries keep twenty-one monks, upper abbeys fourteen Daoist priests; each grade reduced by seven; all select those of practice; the rest returned to be common people."
translations.idiomatic: Your servant asks to grade monasteries in three ranks and abbeys in two: upper monasteries keep twenty-one monks, upper abbeys fourteen priests, each lower rank reduced by seven; select only the devout and return the rest to common life."

sentences.zh: 德宗善之，以為不止本道，可為天下法，乃下尚書省雜議。

translations.literal: Dezong approved it, holding that it was not limited to this circuit but could be a model for the realm, and sent it down to the Department of State Affairs for mixed discussion.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong approved it, holding that the plan could serve as a model for the whole realm, and referred it to the Department of State Affairs for discussion.

sentences.zh: 於是都官員外郎彭偃曰：「王者之政，變人心為上，因人心次之，不變不因為下。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Vice Director of the Capital Bureau Peng Yan said: "The kingly government's policy: transforming people's hearts is highest, following people's hearts next, neither transforming nor following is lowest.
translations.idiomatic: The Capital Bureau vice director Peng Yan said: "In royal government, transforming hearts is best, following hearts second, and neither is worst.

sentences.zh: 今道士有名亡實，欲鮮歸重，於亂政輕；

translations.literal: Now Daoist priests have name without substance, wishing to return to freshness and weight—light in troubled government;
translations.idiomatic: Daoist priests today have names but no substance, seeking a return to purity yet slighting troubled government;

sentences.zh: 僧尼帑穢，皆天下不逞，茍避征役，於亂人甚。

translations.literal: Buddhist monks and nuns are purse-filth; all are the unbridled under heaven, who shirk conscription—very much among the disorderly people.
translations.idiomatic: Buddhist monks and nuns are a drain on the treasury; they are the unruly of the realm who shirk conscription—among the most disorderly of men.

sentences.zh: 今叔明之請雖善，然未能變人心，亦非因人心者。

translations.literal: Now Shuming's request is good, yet it cannot transform people's hearts, nor is it following people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Shuming's proposal is sound, yet it neither transforms hearts nor follows them.

sentences.zh: 夫天生蒸人，必將有職；

translations.literal: Heaven born the multitude of people—they must have occupations;
translations.idiomatic: Heaven gave birth to the multitude; each must have a calling;

sentences.zh: 遊閑浮食，王制所禁。

translations.literal: wandering idleness and floating consumption are forbidden by royal institutions.
translations.idiomatic: idleness and unearned consumption are forbidden by royal law.

sentences.zh: 故賢者受爵祿，不肖者出租稅，古常道也。

translations.literal: Thus the worthy receive ranks and salaries, the unworthy pay rent and tax—ancient constant principle.
translations.idiomatic: The worthy receive rank and salary, the unworthy pay taxes—this is the ancient constant.

sentences.zh: 今僧、道士不耕而食，不織而衣，一僧衣食，歲無慮三萬，五夫所不能致。

translations.literal: Now monks and Daoist priests do not plow yet eat, do not weave yet clothe; one monk's food and clothing, yearly no less than thirty thousand—what five husbands cannot provide.
translations.idiomatic: Monks and priests neither plow nor weave, yet eat and clothe themselves; one monk's yearly upkeep is no less than thirty thousand—more than five households can provide.

sentences.zh: 舉一僧以計天下，其費不貲。

translations.literal: Take one monk to calculate the realm—the expense is beyond reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: Extrapolate from one monk to the realm, and the cost is beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 臣謂僧、道士年未滿五十，可令歲輸絹四，尼及女官輸絹二，雜役與民同之；

translations.literal: Your servant proposes that monks and priests under fifty be required yearly to deliver four bolts of silk, nuns and female officials two, and miscellaneous labor duties the same as common people;
translations.idiomatic: I propose that monks and priests under fifty pay four bolts of silk yearly, nuns and female officials two, and perform the same miscellaneous labor as ordinary subjects;

sentences.zh: 過五十者免。

translations.literal: those over fifty be exempt.
translations.idiomatic: those over fifty should be exempt.

sentences.zh: 凡人年五十，嗜欲已衰，況有戒法以檢其性情哉！」

translations.literal: When people reach fifty, desires already decline—how much more when discipline and law restrain their nature!"
translations.idiomatic: At fifty human desires already fade—how much more when religious discipline restrains the temperament!"

sentences.zh: 刑部員外郎裴伯言曰：「衣者，蠶桑也；

translations.literal: The Vice Director of Punishments Pei Boyan said: "Clothing comes from mulberry and silkworm;
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director of Punishments Pei Boyan said, "Clothing comes from sericulture;

sentences.zh: 食者，耕農也；

translations.literal: food comes from plowing and farming;
translations.idiomatic: food comes from farming;

sentences.zh: 男女者，繼祖之重也。

translations.literal: men and women are the weight of continuing the ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: men and women carry the weight of continuing the ancestral line.

sentences.zh: 而二教悉禁，國家著令，又從而助之，是以夷狄不經法反制中夏禮義之俗也。

translations.literal: Yet both teachings forbid them entirely, and the state issues orders further aiding them—thus barbarians who do not follow the law in turn control the customs of Central Xia's ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Yet both faiths forbid them, and the state issues orders that further aid them—so foreign teachings that ignore law end up governing the ritual customs of the Central Plains.

sentences.zh: 傳曰：『女子十四有為人母之道，四十九絕生育之理；

translations.literal: The tradition says: 'A woman at fourteen has the way of becoming a mother; at forty-nine the principle of bearing ends;'
translations.idiomatic: Tradition says, 'At fourteen a woman is fit to become a mother; at forty-nine the principle of childbearing ends;'

sentences.zh: 男子十六有為人父之道，六十四絕陽化之理。』

translations.literal: a man at sixteen has the way of becoming a father; at sixty-four the principle of yang transformation ends.
translations.idiomatic: at sixteen a man is fit to become a father; at sixty-four the principle of yang transformation ends.

sentences.zh: 臣請僧、道士一切限年六十四以上，尼、女官四十九以上，許終身在道，餘悉還為編人，官為計口授地，收廢寺觀以為廬舍。」

translations.literal: Your servant asks that all monks and priests be limited to age sixty-four and above, nuns and female officials forty-nine and above, permitted to remain in the Way for life; the rest all returned to registered commoners, the government allotting land by head count, and abandoned temples and abbeys taken as lodging."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that monks and priests be limited to those sixty-four and older, nuns and female officials forty-nine and older, allowed to remain in orders for life; all others returned to the registers, land allotted by household, and abandoned temples converted to lodging."

sentences.zh: 議雖上，罷之。

translations.literal: Although the discussion was submitted, it was set aside.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was submitted but shelved.

sentences.zh: 子昇，以少卿從德宗梁州。

translations.literal: Sheng, as Junior Mentor, followed Dezong to Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His son Sheng, as Junior Mentor, accompanied Dezong to Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 叔明嚴敕以死報，故昇有功，擢禁軍將軍。

translations.literal: Shuming sternly ordered him to repay with his life; thus Sheng had merit and was promoted to a general of the Palace Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Shuming sternly ordered him to repay with his life; Sheng distinguished himself and was promoted to a Palace Guard general.

sentences.zh: 貞元初，遷太子詹事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenyuan he was transferred to Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenyuan he became Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 坐郜國公主，貶羅州別駕。

translations.literal: For involvement with Princess Guo, he was demoted to vice prefect of Luo.
translations.idiomatic: For ties to Princess Guo, he was demoted to vice prefect of Luo.

sentences.zh: 叔明素豪侈，在蜀殖財，廣第舍田產。

translations.literal: Shuming had always been extravagant; in Shu he amassed wealth, with broad mansions, fields, and estates.
translations.idiomatic: Shuming had always lived lavishly; in Shu he amassed wealth, with grand estates and broad holdings.

sentences.zh: 歿數年，子孫驕縱，貲產皆盡。

translations.literal: Several years after his death, his descendants grew arrogant and dissolute until assets were exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Within years of his death his descendants grew arrogant and dissolute, and the family fortune was spent.

sentences.zh: 世言多藏者以叔明為鑒雲。

translations.literal: The age says those who hoard much take Shuming as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: People say those who hoard great wealth should take Shuming as a warning.

sentences.zh: 曲環，陜州安邑人，客隴右。

translations.literal: Qu Huan was a native of Anyi in Shaanzhou, registered as a guest in Longyou.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Huan was from Anyi in Shaanzhou and had registered in Longyou.

sentences.zh: 少喜兵法，資勇敢，善騎射。

translations.literal: In youth he delighted in military arts, was naturally brave, and skilled in mounted archery.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he loved military arts, was naturally brave, and skilled in mounted archery.

sentences.zh: 天寶中，從哥舒翰討吐蕃，拔石堡，取黃河九曲洪濟等城，授果毅別將。

translations.literal: In Tianbao he followed Geshu Han against Tibet, captured Stone Fortress, took the Yellow River's nine bends and Hongji and other cities, and was appointed resolute separate commander.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianbao he followed Geshu Han against Tibet, captured Stone Fortress, took the nine bends of the Yellow River and cities including Hongji, and was made resolute separate commander.

sentences.zh: 安祿山反，從魯炅守鄧州，與賊武令珣戰尤力，加左清道率。

translations.literal: When An Lushan rebelled, he followed Lu Jiong in defending Dengzhou, fought Wu Lingxun with especial force, and was made Left Purification Commander.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan rebelled, he followed Lu Jiong in defending Dengzhou, fought Wu Lingxun fiercely, and was made Left Purification Commander.

sentences.zh: 從李抱玉屯河陽。

translations.literal: He followed Li Baoyu in garrisoning Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: He garrisoned Heyang under Li Baoyu.

sentences.zh: 又自將兵守澤州，破賊銳將安曉，拜羽林將軍。

translations.literal: He also personally led troops to defend Zezhou, defeated the rebel elite general An Xiao, and was appointed General of the Forest Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He also commanded troops at Zezhou, defeated the rebel elite An Xiao, and was made General of the Forest Guard.

sentences.zh: 與諸將討史朝義，平河北，累轉金吾大將軍。

translations.literal: With the generals he campaigned against Shi Chaoyi and pacified Hebei, rising repeatedly to Grand General of the Gold Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the generals against Shi Chaoyi, pacified Hebei, and rose to Grand General of the Gold Guard.

sentences.zh: 大歷中，戍隴州，數破吐蕃，以功兼太常卿。

translations.literal: In the Dali era he garrisoned Longzhou, repeatedly defeated Tibet, and for merit was additionally made Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: In the Dali era he garrisoned Longzhou, repeatedly defeated Tibet, and was made Minister of Ceremonies for his merit.

sentences.zh: 德宗初，虜寇劍南，詔環以邠、隴兵五千馳救，收七盤城、威武軍、維茂等州，虜破走，威名大振，加太子賓客，賜名馬。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dezong's reign, when barbarians raided Jiannan, Huan was ordered with five thousand Bing and Long troops to rush to the rescue; he recovered Qipan City, Weiwu Army, Weimao, and other prefectures; the barbarians were routed and fled; his fame greatly shook; he was made Guest of the Heir Apparent and given a famous horse.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Dezong's reign, when invaders raided Jiannan, Huan was sent with five thousand Bing and Long troops, recovered Qipan City, Weiwu Army, Weimao, and other prefectures, routed the enemy, and won great fame; he was made Guest of the Heir Apparent and given a famous horse.

sentences.zh: 豫討涇州劉文喜，遷開府儀同三司，封晉昌郡王，邠隴兵馬使。

translations.literal: In the planned campaign against Liu Wenxi of Jingzhou, he was transferred to Grand Master with privileges equal to the Three Excellencies, enfeoffed Prince of Jinchang, and made Bing-Long military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the campaign against Liu Wenxi of Jingzhou he was made Grand Master equal to the Three Excellencies, enfeoffed Prince of Jinchang, and made Bing-Long military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 時李納逼徐州，環與劉玄佐救之，敗其眾，功最。

translations.literal: When Li Na pressed Xuzhou, Huan with Liu Xuanzuo relieved it, defeated his forces, and had the greatest merit.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Na pressed Xuzhou, Huan and Liu Xuanzuo relieved the city, defeated his army, and won the greatest credit.

sentences.zh: 建中三年，擢邠隴行營節度使。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianzhong he was promoted to commissioner of the Bing-Long field army.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianzhong year 3 he was made commissioner of the Bing-Long field army.

sentences.zh: 李希烈陷汴州，環守寧陵，戰陳州，斬賊三萬五千級，禽其將翟崇暉，進檢校工部尚書，兼陳州刺史。

translations.literal: When Li Xilie captured Bianzhou, Huan defended Ningling, fought at Chenzhou, beheaded thirty-five thousand rebels, captured the general Zhai Chonghui, and was made Acting Minister of Works and concurrently prefect of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Xilie took Bianzhou, Huan defended Ningling, fought at Chenzhou, killed thirty-five thousand rebels, captured Zhai Chonghui, and was made Acting Minister of Works and prefect of Chen.

sentences.zh: 希烈平，改陳許節度，賜封三百戶。

translations.literal: When Xilie was pacified, he was made commissioner of Chen and Xu and granted an income of three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: After Xilie was pacified, he was made commissioner of Chen and Xu with an income of three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 二州比為寇沖，民苦剽鹵，客他縣。

translations.literal: The two prefectures had long been on the bandit frontier; the people suffered plunder and fled to other counties.
translations.idiomatic: The two prefectures had long been on the frontier of raids; people suffered plunder and fled elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 環勤身節用，寬賦斂，簡條教，不三歲，歸者繦系。

translations.literal: Huan worked diligently and lived frugally, lightened taxes and levies, simplified regulations and instruction, and within three years returnees were linked in strings.
translations.idiomatic: Huan worked tirelessly, lived frugally, eased taxes, simplified regulations, and within three years refugees returned in droves.

sentences.zh: 訓農治兵，谷食豐衍。

translations.literal: He trained farmers and drilled troops until grain was abundant.
translations.idiomatic: He trained farmers and soldiers until grain stores overflowed.

sentences.zh: 轉檢校尚書左仆射。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Acting Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Acting Left Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 貞元十五年，卒，年七十四，贈司空。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Zhenyuan he died at seventy-four and was posthumously made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyuan year 15 he died at seventy-four and was posthumously made Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 王虔休，字君佐，汝州梁人。
