translations.literal: Wang Qianxiu was styled Junzuo, a native of Liang in Ruzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qianxiu, styled Junzuo, was from Liang in Ruzhou.

sentences.zh: 少涉學，有材武，以信義為鄉黨畏慕。

translations.literal: In youth he studied somewhat, had martial talent, and for faith and righteousness was feared and admired in his district.
translations.idiomatic: He studied in youth, had martial talent, and was respected locally for faith and righteousness.

sentences.zh: 大歷中，刺史李深署為裨將。

translations.literal: In the Dali era Prefect Li Shen appointed him as adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: In the Dali era Prefect Li Shen made him adjutant.

sentences.zh: 澤潞李抱真聞其名，厚以幣招之，授兵馬使。

translations.literal: Li Baozhen of Zelu heard his name and recruited him generously, appointing him military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Li Baozhen of Zelu heard of him, recruited him generously, and made him military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 抱真討河北，戰雙罔、臨洺，虔休以多擢步軍都虞候，封同昌郡王，實封五十戶。

translations.literal: In Baozhen's Hebei campaign, fighting at Shuangwang and Linming, Qianxiu was repeatedly promoted for merit to Chief of Infantry of the Army and enfeoffed Duke of Tongchang with a substantive fief of fifty households.
translations.idiomatic: In Baozhen's Hebei campaigns at Shuangwang and Linming, Qianxiu rose to Chief of Infantry and was enfeoffed Duke of Tongchang with fifty households.

sentences.zh: 抱真卒，元仲經等謀樹其子緘，一軍思亂，虔休正色語眾曰：「軍，王軍；

translations.literal: After Baozhen's death, Yuan Zhongjing and others plotted to install his son Jian; the whole army thought of mutiny. Qianxiu said sternly to the crowd: "The army is the prince's army;
translations.idiomatic: After Baozhen died, Yuan Zhongjing and others plotted to install his son Jian and the army nearly mutinied. Qianxiu said sternly, "This army belongs to the throne;

sentences.zh: 州，王土也。

translations.literal: the prefecture is the prince's land.
translations.idiomatic: this land belongs to the throne.

sentences.zh: 帥亡當稟天子，何云云有妄謀？」

translations.literal: When the commander dies one should report to the Son of Heaven—why these reckless schemes?"
translations.idiomatic: When the commander dies we report to the emperor—why talk of reckless schemes?"

sentences.zh: 眾服其言，得不亂。

translations.literal: The crowd accepted his words and disorder was avoided.
translations.idiomatic: The men accepted his words and disorder was averted.

sentences.zh: 德宗嘉之，以邕王為昭義節度大使，擢虔休潞州左司馬，領留後。

translations.literal: Dezong praised him; the Prince of Yong was made supreme commissioner of Zhaoyi; Qianxiu was promoted to Left Marshal of Luzhou and acting commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong praised him, made the Prince of Yong supreme commissioner of Zhaoyi, and promoted Qianxiu to Left Marshal of Luzhou as acting commissioner.

sentences.zh: 本名延貴，至是賜名。

translations.literal: His original name was Yanging; at this time he was granted his new name.
translations.idiomatic: His original name was Yanging; he was then granted his new name.

sentences.zh: 號令撫循，軍中大治。

translations.literal: His orders comforted and his governance settled the army; the army was greatly well ordered.
translations.idiomatic: His orders reassured the men and the army was brought to excellent order.

sentences.zh: 初，抱真之喪，軍司馬元誼據洺州叛，虔休遣將李廷芝討之，戰長橋，斬級數百；

translations.literal: At first, after Baozhen's mourning, the army marshal Yuan Yi held Luozhou in rebellion; Qianxiu sent General Li Tingzhi against him; at Chang Bridge he beheaded several hundred;
translations.idiomatic: After Baozhen's death, army marshal Yuan Yi rebelled at Luozhou; Qianxiu sent Li Tingzhi against him and at Chang Bridge beheaded hundreds;

sentences.zh: 次雞澤，又破之。

translations.literal: next at Jize he defeated him again.
translations.idiomatic: then defeated him again at Jize.

sentences.zh: 守戍皆奔魏博，即決水灌城，將壞，遣掌書記盧頊入見誼，陳利害。

translations.literal: The garrison all fled to Weibo; he then breached the dyke to flood the city, which was about to collapse; he sent Recorder Lu Qi to see Yi and explain advantage and harm.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison fled to Weibo; he breached the dyke to flood the city, which was near collapse, and sent recorder Lu Qi to explain the stakes to Yi.

sentences.zh: 誼請朝，即以頊為洺州別駕，使守洺。

translations.literal: Yi asked to come to court; Qi was immediately made vice prefect of Luo to hold the city.
translations.idiomatic: Yi asked to submit to court; Qi was made vice prefect of Luo to hold the city.

sentences.zh: 誼出，亦奔魏。

translations.literal: When Yi came out, he too fled to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: When Yi emerged, he too fled to Wei.

sentences.zh: 治潞二歲，遷昭義節度使，檢校工部尚書。

translations.literal: After governing Lu for two years, he was transferred to Zhaoyi commissioner and Acting Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: After two years governing Lu he was made Zhaoyi commissioner and Acting Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 始，屬城州縣守宰多署它職，不親政，故治茍簡。

translations.literal: At first, in subordinate prefectures and counties many magistrates held other posts and did not attend to government, so administration was perfunctory.
translations.idiomatic: Previously many county magistrates held other posts and neglected government, so administration was lax.

sentences.zh: 虔休悉增俸稟，遣就部，人以妥安。

translations.literal: Qianxiu increased all salaries and sent them to their posts; people felt secure.
translations.idiomatic: Qianxiu raised salaries and sent officials to their posts; the people felt secure.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十三，贈尚書左仆射，謚曰敬。

translations.literal: He died at sixty-three and was posthumously made Left Vice Director with the posthumous title Reverent.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-three and was posthumously made Left Vice Director with the title Reverent.

sentences.zh: 虔休性恪敏，節用度，既沒，所部帑廩皆可支數歲。

translations.literal: Qianxiu was by nature diligent and frugal; after his death the treasury stores of his command could support several years.
translations.idiomatic: Diligent and frugal by nature, after his death his command's treasury could support the region for years.

sentences.zh: 嘗得太常樂家劉玠撰《繼天誕聖樂》，因帝誕日以獻。

translations.literal: He once obtained the Court of Imperial Sacrifices musician Liu Jie's composition "Music Continuing Heaven and Celebrating Sagely Birth" and presented it on the emperor's birthday.
translations.idiomatic: He obtained court musician Liu Jie's "Music Continuing Heaven and Celebrating Sagely Birth" and presented it on the emperor's birthday.

sentences.zh: 其樂，以宮為均，示五聲有君也；

translations.literal: The music takes the gong mode as its standard, showing that among the five tones there is a lord;
translations.idiomatic: The music used the gong mode as standard, showing the five tones have a sovereign;

sentences.zh: 以土為德，本五運在中也；

translations.literal: takes earth as virtue, rooted in the five cycles at the center;
translations.idiomatic: used earth as virtue, rooted in the five phases at the center;

sentences.zh: 奏二十五疊，取二十四氣而成一歲；

translations.literal: performs twenty-five repetitions, taking the twenty-four qi to complete one year;
translations.idiomatic: performed twenty-five repetitions for the twenty-four seasonal nodes of a year;

sentences.zh: 奏十六節，象元、凱登庸於朝雲。

translations.literal: performs sixteen sections, symbolizing primal virtue and triumphant accession at morning clouds.
translations.idiomatic: performed sixteen sections symbolizing primal virtue and triumphant accession.

sentences.zh: 後《中和樂》本於此。

translations.literal: Later the "Music of Central Harmony" derived from this.
translations.idiomatic: Later the "Music of Central Harmony" derived from it.

sentences.zh: 子麗成等十人，並補太學生。

translations.literal: His sons Lincheng and nine others were all appointed students of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Lincheng and nine others were all appointed Imperial Academy students.

sentences.zh: 盧群，字載初，系出范陽。

translations.literal: Lu Qun was styled Zaichu and traced his line to Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Qun, styled Zaichu, traced his line to Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 少學於垂山，淮南陳少遊聞其名，奏署幕府，已而薦諸朝。

translations.literal: In youth he studied at Chuishan; Chen Shaoyou of Huainan heard his name, memorialized appointing him to his staff, and later recommended him to court.
translations.idiomatic: He studied at Chuishan in youth; Chen Shaoyou of Huainan recruited him to his staff and later recommended him at court.

sentences.zh: 李希烈反，以監察御史為江西行營糧料使。

translations.literal: When Li Xilie rebelled, he was made grain supply commissioner of the Jiangxi field army as Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Xilie rebelled he was made Palace Attendant and grain commissioner of the Jiangxi field army.

sentences.zh: 嗣曹王臯節度江西，奏為判官。

translations.literal: When Prince of Succession Cao Wang Gao held Jiangxi, he memorialized appointing Qun as aide.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Succession Cao Wang Gao, as Jiangxi commissioner, made him aide.

sentences.zh: 臯徙荊襄，皆從其府，以勁正聞。

translations.literal: When Gao moved to Jing and Xiang, Qun followed his staff in both places and was known for firm uprightness.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao moved to Jing and Xiang, Qun followed him and was known for firm integrity.

sentences.zh: 入為侍御史。

translations.literal: He entered service as Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital as Attending Censor.

sentences.zh: 郭子儀家與嬖人張昆弟訟財不平，又言嬖人宅匿珍寶。

translations.literal: In Guo Ziyi's household, Ziyi and his favorite Zhang Kun sued one another over property, and it was also said the favorite's residence concealed treasures.
translations.idiomatic: In Guo Ziyi's household, Ziyi and his favorite Zhang Kun sued over property, and it was said the favorite's house concealed treasure.

sentences.zh: 德宗促按之。

translations.literal: Dezong urged a swift investigation.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong ordered a swift investigation.

sentences.zh: 群奏言：「子儀有大勛德，今所訟皆其家事，且嬖人宅，子儀昔畀之，非子弟所宜言，請赦勿問。」

translations.literal: Qun memorialized: "Ziyi has great merit and virtue; what is now litigated is all his household affair, and moreover the favorite's residence—Ziyi once gave it to him; it is not fitting for sons and nephews to speak of it. I ask that it be pardoned and not investigated."
translations.idiomatic: Qun memorialized, "Ziyi has immense merit; this dispute is a family matter, and the favorite's house was once given him by Ziyi—not something sons and nephews should raise. I ask that the case be dropped."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 人謂群識大體。

translations.literal: People said Qun understood the larger pattern.
translations.idiomatic: People praised Qun for grasping the larger interest.

sentences.zh: 累遷兵部郎中。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly transferred to Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 淮西吳少誠擅決司洧水溉田，使者止之，不奉詔。

translations.literal: In Huaixi, Wu Shaoqing on his own authority decided to irrigate fields with the Si and Wei rivers; envoys stopped him but he would not obey the edict.
translations.idiomatic: In Huaixi, Wu Shaoqing on his own authority diverted the Si and Wei rivers to irrigate fields; envoys stopped him but he refused the edict.

sentences.zh: 命群臨詰，少誠曰：「是於人有利。」

translations.literal: Qun was ordered to go and question him; Shaoqing said: "This benefits the people."
translations.idiomatic: Qun was sent to question him; Shaoqing said, "This benefits the people."

sentences.zh: 群曰：「臣道貴順，恭恪所以為順也。

translations.literal: Qun said: "The way of a minister values compliance; respect and reverence are what compliance means.
translations.idiomatic: Qun said, "A minister's way values compliance; respect and reverence are compliance.

sentences.zh: 專命廢順，雖利何有？

translations.literal: Arbitrary orders abandon compliance—what good is benefit?
translations.idiomatic: Private orders abandon compliance—what good is benefit?

sentences.zh: 且怠於事上者，固不能責其下矣。」

translations.literal: Moreover, one who is slack toward his superiors surely cannot demand obedience from subordinates."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, one slack toward superiors cannot demand obedience below."

sentences.zh: 少誠聽命。

translations.literal: Shaoqing obeyed the order.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoqing obeyed.

sentences.zh: 群又為陳古今成敗事，逆順禍福皆有效，所以感動之，少誠竦然。

translations.literal: Qun also set forth ancient and modern successes and failures; whether contrary or compliant, fortune and calamity all had effect, thereby moving him; Shaoqing was startled.
translations.idiomatic: Qun also recounted ancient and modern successes and failures, showing how loyalty and defiance brought fortune or ruin, and moved him deeply; Shaoqing was startled.

sentences.zh: 既置酒，與賦詩，又歌以慰之。

translations.literal: When wine was set out, they composed poems together, and he also sang to comfort him.
translations.idiomatic: Over wine they composed poems, and Qun sang to comfort him.

sentences.zh: 少誠感悅，不敢桀。

translations.literal: Shaoqing was moved and pleased and did not dare act arrogantly.
translations.idiomatic: Moved and pleased, Shaoqing no longer acted arrogantly.

sentences.zh: 以奉使稱旨，遷檢校秘書監、鄭滑節度行軍司馬。

translations.literal: For fulfilling his mission as the emperor wished, he was transferred to Acting Director of the Palace Library and field army marshal of Zheng and Hua.
translations.idiomatic: For fulfilling his mission he was made Acting Director of the Palace Library and field marshal of Zheng and Hua.

sentences.zh: 姚南仲入朝，即以群代節度。

translations.literal: When Yao Nanzhong entered court, Qun replaced him as commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Yao Nanzhong came to court, Qun replaced him as commissioner.

sentences.zh: 群嘗客於鄭，質良田以耕。

translations.literal: Qun had once been a guest in Zheng and pledged good fields to farm.
translations.idiomatic: He had once been a guest in Zheng and pledged good fields to farm.

sentences.zh: 至是則出券貸直，以田歸其人。

translations.literal: Now he produced the pledge and loaned its value, returning the fields to their owner.
translations.idiomatic: Now he produced the pledge, repaid its value, and returned the land to the owner.

sentences.zh: 卒，年五十九，贈工部尚書。

translations.literal: He died at fifty-nine and was posthumously made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He died at fifty-nine and was posthumously honored as Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 李元素，字大樸，邢國公密裔孫，仕為御史。

translations.literal: Li Yuansu was styled Dapu, a descendant of Duke Mi of Xing, and served as censor.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuansu, styled Dapu, was a descendant of Duke Mi of Xing and served as censor.

sentences.zh: 東都留守杜亞惡大將令狐運，會盜劫輸絹於洛北，運適與其下畋近郊，亞疑而訊之。

translations.literal: Eastern Capital defender Du Ya hated the great general Linghu Yun; when bandits robbed silk shipments north of Luo, Yun happened to be hunting with his men near the suburbs, and Ya suspected and interrogated him.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Capital defender Du Ya hated great general Linghu Yun; when bandits robbed silk north of Luo, Yun happened to be hunting nearby, and Ya suspected and interrogated him.

sentences.zh: 幕府穆員、張弘靖按鞫無狀，亞怒，更以愛將武金掠服之，死者甚眾。

translations.literal: Staff members Mu Yuan and Zhang Hongjing investigated and found no evidence; Ya grew angry and had his favorite general Wu Jin torture confessions until many died.
translations.idiomatic: Staff members Mu Yuan and Zhang Hongjing found no evidence; Ya grew angry and had favorite general Wu Jin torture confessions until many died.

sentences.zh: 亞請斥運醜土，詔監察御史楊寧覆驗，事皆不讎。

translations.literal: Ya asked to exile Yun to remote soil; the edict ordered Attending Censor Yang Ning to reverify; nothing matched.
translations.idiomatic: Ya asked to exile Yun; censor Yang Ning was ordered to reverify and found no match.

sentences.zh: 亞怒，劾寧罔上，寧抵罪。

translations.literal: Ya grew angry, impeached Ning for deceiving the throne, and Ning was punished.
translations.idiomatic: Ya impeached Ning for deceiving the throne, and Ning was punished.

sentences.zh: 又自以不失盜為功，因必其怒，傅致而周內之，若不可翻者。

translations.literal: He also held that not losing the stolen goods was merit, and therefore insisted on his rage, fabricating charges and encircling Yun within them as though the case could not be overturned.
translations.idiomatic: He also treated recovering none of the goods as success, clung to his rage, fabricated charges, and boxed Yun in as if the case could not be overturned.

sentences.zh: 德宗信不疑，宰相難之。

translations.literal: Dezong believed without doubt; the chief ministers found it difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong believed him without question; the chief ministers objected.

sentences.zh: 詔元素與刑部員外郎崔從質、大理司直盧士瞻馳按，亞迎，以獄告。

translations.literal: Yuansu was ordered with Vice Director of Punishments Cui Congzhi and Director of the Court of Judicial Review Lu Shizhan to rush and investigate; Ya met them and presented the case.
translations.idiomatic: Yuansu was ordered with Cui Congzhi of Punishments and Lu Shizhan of Judicial Review to investigate; Ya met them and presented the case.

sentences.zh: 元素徐察其冤，悉縱所囚以還。

translations.literal: Yuansu slowly investigated the injustice and released all prisoners to return.
translations.idiomatic: Yuansu slowly uncovered the injustice and released all the prisoners.

sentences.zh: 亞大驚，復劾元素失有罪。

translations.literal: Ya was greatly alarmed and again impeached Yuansu for releasing the guilty.
translations.idiomatic: Ya was alarmed and again impeached Yuansu for freeing the guilty.

sentences.zh: 比元素還，帝已怒，奏獄未畢，帝曰：「出。」

translations.literal: By the time Yuansu returned, the emperor was already angry; the memorial on the case was not finished when the emperor said: "Withdraw."
translations.idiomatic: Before Yuansu returned, the emperor was already angry; the report was unfinished when the emperor said, "Withdraw."

sentences.zh: 元素曰：「臣言有所未盡。」

translations.literal: Yuansu said: "Your servant's words are not yet complete."
translations.idiomatic: Yuansu said, "I have not finished speaking."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「第去。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Just go."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Go."

sentences.zh: 元素曰：「臣以御史按獄，知冤不得盡辭，是無容復見陛下。」

translations.literal: Yuansu said: "Your servant as censor investigated the case and knows the injustice could not be fully spoken—there is no face to see Your Majesty again."
translations.idiomatic: Yuansu said, "As censor I found injustice that could not be fully stated—I have no face to see Your Majesty again."

sentences.zh: 帝意解，即道運冤狀。

translations.literal: The emperor's mind eased and Yuansu immediately set forth Yun's grievance.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor relented, and Yuansu laid out Yun's grievance.

sentences.zh: 帝感寤曰：「非卿，孰能辨之？」

translations.literal: The emperor, moved to understanding, said: "Without you, who could have distinguished it?"
translations.idiomatic: Moved, the emperor said, "Without you, who could have seen this?"

sentences.zh: 然運猶以擅捕人得罪，流歸州，死於貶。

translations.literal: Yet Yun was still punished for unauthorized arrest of people, exiled to Guizhou, and died in banishment.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Yun was still punished for unauthorized arrests, exiled to Guizhou, and died in banishment.

sentences.zh: 武金流建州。

translations.literal: Wu Jin was exiled to Jianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jin was exiled to Jianzhou.

sentences.zh: 後歲餘，齊抗得真盜，繇是天下重之。

translations.literal: More than a year later Qi Kang captured the real bandits; from this the realm esteemed Yuansu.
translations.idiomatic: More than a year later Qi Kang caught the real bandits, and the realm esteemed Yuansu.

sentences.zh: 遷給事中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Attendant of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Attendant of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 後美官缺，鹹冀元素得其處。

translations.literal: Later when fine offices were vacant, all hoped Yuansu would obtain them.
translations.idiomatic: When fine offices opened, all hoped Yuansu would fill them.

sentences.zh: 會鄭滑節度使盧群卒，拜元素檢校工部尚書節度其軍，治有異績。

translations.literal: When Zheng and Hua commissioner Lu Qun died, Yuansu was appointed Acting Minister of Works and commissioner of that army; his governance had unusual achievement.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Qun died as Zheng and Hua commissioner, Yuansu was made Acting Minister of Works and commissioner, with notable achievements.

sentences.zh: 元和初，召為御史大夫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanhe he was summoned as Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Yuanhe he was summoned as Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 大夫，自貞元後難其人不補，而元素以夙望召拜，中外企聽風采。

translations.literal: The post of Censor-in-Chief had been hard to fill since Zhenyuan for lack of suitable men, yet Yuansu was summoned and appointed for long-standing reputation; inside and outside the court awaited his bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Since Zhenyuan the post of Censor-in-Chief had gone unfilled for lack of suitable men; Yuansu was summoned for his reputation, and court and country awaited his bearing.

sentences.zh: 既而一不建為，容容持祿，內望作宰相。

translations.literal: Yet he accomplished nothing, held his salary with easy compliance, and inwardly hoped to become chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he accomplished nothing, coasted on his salary, and inwardly hoped to become chief minister.

sentences.zh: 久之不見用，則謝賓客曰：「無以官散外我。」

translations.literal: After long failure to be used, he told his guests: "Do not cast me out with an honorary post in the provinces."
translations.idiomatic: After long disuse he told guests, "Do not park me in an honorary provincial post."

sentences.zh: 見屬吏輒先拜，人人失望。

translations.literal: When he saw subordinate officials he bowed first; everyone was disappointed.
translations.idiomatic: He bowed first to subordinate officials, to everyone's disappointment.

sentences.zh: 李锜反，拜浙西節度使。

translations.literal: When Li Qi rebelled, he was appointed Zhexi commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Qi rebelled, he was made Zhexi commissioner.

sentences.zh: 數月還，為國子祭酒，進戶部尚書、判度支。

translations.literal: After several months he returned and was made Chancellor of the National University, advanced to Minister of Revenue and concurrently director of fiscal affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He returned after months as Chancellor of the National University, then Minister of Revenue and fiscal director.

sentences.zh: 元素少孤，奉長姊謹悌，及沒，悲鯁成疾，因辭職屏居。

translations.literal: Yuansu was orphaned young, served his elder sister with reverent brotherly duty, and when she died grief lodged in him as illness; he therefore resigned and lived in seclusion.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he served his elder sister devotedly; her death brought grief that became illness, and he resigned to live in seclusion.

sentences.zh: 其妻，石泉公王方慶之孫。

translations.literal: His wife was granddaughter of Duke of Shiquan Wang Fangqing.
translations.idiomatic: His wife was a granddaughter of Duke of Shiquan Wang Fangqing.

sentences.zh: 前妻子皆不肖，而元素溺姬侍，王不見答。

translations.literal: Sons by a former wife were all unworthy, yet Yuansu doted on concubines; the Wang family received no reply.
translations.idiomatic: His sons by a former wife were worthless, yet he doted on concubines and ignored his Wang wife.

sentences.zh: 元素久疾，益昏惑，遂出之。

translations.literal: Yuansu was long ill and grew increasingly confused, and finally sent her away.
translations.idiomatic: Long ill, he grew confused and finally divorced her.

sentences.zh: 王訴諸朝，詔免元素官，且令畀王貲五百萬。

translations.literal: Wang appealed to court; an edict removed Yuansu from office and ordered him to give Wang five million in assets.
translations.idiomatic: Wang appealed; an edict stripped Yuansu of office and ordered five million in assets paid her.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈陜州大都督。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously made Grand Protector of Shaanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously honored as Grand Protector of Shaanzhou.

sentences.zh: 盧士玫者，山東人。

translations.literal: Lu Shimei was a man of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Shimei was from Shandong.

sentences.zh: 以文儒進，端厚無競。

translations.literal: He advanced through literary learning, was upright and thick and without contention.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through letters, was upright, steady, and uncontentious.

sentences.zh: 為吏部員外郎，善於職。

translations.literal: As Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel he was skilled in his duties.
translations.idiomatic: As Vice Director of Personnel he excelled at his duties.

sentences.zh: 再遷知京兆尹。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to acting mayor of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made acting mayor of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 劉總入朝，與士玫故內姻，乃請析瀛、鄚兩州，用士玫為觀察使。

translations.literal: When Liu Zong entered court, being old affines with Shimei, he asked to split Ying and Mo prefectures and appoint Shimei observation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Zong came to court, an old family connection, he asked to split Ying and Mo and make Shimei observation commissioner.

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved the request.

sentences.zh: 俄而幽州亂，朱克融襲之，朝廷欲重其任，就加節度使。

translations.literal: Soon Youzhou fell into disorder; Zhu Keyong attacked; the court wished to weight his responsibility and additionally made him military commissioner on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Youzhou rebelled and Zhu Keyong attacked; the court added the military commission on the spot to weight his authority.

sentences.zh: 士玫空家貲助軍，然部卒多家幽州，陰導克融入，故士玫闔府皆見囚幽州。

translations.literal: Shimei emptied family wealth to aid the army, but many of his troops were from Youzhou and secretly guided Keyong in; thus Shimei's whole staff were imprisoned in Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shimei spent his family wealth on the army, but many troops were Youzhou men who guided Keyong in, and Shimei's whole staff were seized in Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 天子赦克融，得還。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven pardoned Keyong and they were able to return.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor pardoned Keyong and they returned.

sentences.zh: 以太子賓客分司東都，徐虢州刺史，復為賓客。

translations.literal: He was made Guest of the Heir Apparent with duties at the eastern capital, then prefect of Xu and Guo, and again Guest of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was Guest of the Heir Apparent at Luoyang, then prefect of Xu and Guo, then Guest again.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈工部尚書。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously honored as Minister of Works.
